claimsMade.text: THE SECOND-BEST FINDING IN THIS CLUSTER: TWO PEOPLE REACH THE SAME COUNTER-EXPLANATION BY UNRELATED ROUTES. Tom Mahood, a physics graduate who spent years on the documentary record, concludes in his 2018 retrospective that there is 'nothing at Papoose Lake' and that S-4 actually refers to a radar facility at the Tonopah Test Range. Separately, T.D. Barnes, a former CIA and NASA engineer who worked at Groom Lake, says the real Site 4 is a remote radar site north of the main facility that held captured Soviet equipment, that this and not an underground base is what Lazar referred to, and that a named retired Area 51 security chief confirmed to him that Lazar appears on no manifest. Neither route depends on the other: one is documentary and civilian, the other is recollection by a former range engineer. Shared conclusions from a shared method are not corroboration; these two do not share a method.

label: Tom Mahood
narrative: Tom Mahood is the custody and analysis point for most of the documentary record in this cluster, and without a node for him the board's case-against edges have nothing to originate from. He describes himself on his own site as a former civil engineer and traffic engineer for Orange County, California, with a Master's degree in physics from Cal State Fullerton. His otherhand.org investigation reprints the Los Alamos Monitor front page of 27 June 1982, both Las Vegas Review-Journal reports of 1990, Mark Farmer's 1996 taped interview with an anonymised Los Alamos colleague, and David L. Morgan's physics critique, and it quotes Lazar's 1990 Pre-Sentence Report. His conclusion on the credentials is flat: 'Lazar never attended either CalTech or MIT. Of this I am certain of beyond a reasonable doubt.' His 2018 retrospective is the single best case-against document in the cluster precisely because it concedes what is true, granting that Lazar is 'amazingly believable', that Mahood himself initially found the story plausible, and that Lazar showed genuine technical cleverness. His counter-explanation is that there is nothing at Papoose Lake, that S-4 is a designator attaching to a Tonopah Test Range radar facility, and that the account began as a cover story after security caught Lazar bringing friends to watch classified tests in April 1989.
